source: Rankings from Acquesta, Darling & Nichol, 'Towards Certifying Trustworthy Machine Learning Models for Acoustic Signal Classification' (ASA, May 2026), slide 10. Categories, definitions, and consistency checks are a draft for co-author review.
structure_note: Rankings are independent facets: a project's position is the combination of its answers. Categories inside a ranking can have sub-levels; only leaf categories are selectable, and a method or rule that names a parent applies to all of its children. Where one ranking's answer genuinely constrains another's, the constraint is written as a consistency check below. Those checks are the evidence for deciding whether any part of the taxonomy should become a strict hierarchy.

sections.title: Application context
sections.help: GCMM ties every credibility claim to an intended use, a consequence level, and an operating domain.

questions.label: Intended use
questions.placeholder: What decision or analysis will the model's output feed?

options.label: Moderate
options.hint: Could misdirect work, but no direct safety or policy effect

options.label: Critical
options.hint: High consequence and directly drives critical decisions

questions.label: How will the model be used?

options.label: Decision support with a human reviewing outputs
Acts without a human in the loop

questions.label: The intended use is written down and agreed
The operating domain (conditions, ranges, populations) is written down
Operating conditions are expected to differ from the training data

sections.title: Decision context
sections.help: The mission area the model serves and the kind of decision it informs. Sets which domain experts are needed.

options.label: Structural health & NDE
options.definition: Detecting, locating, or characterizing damage and degradation in engineered structures and components.

options.label: Climate & Earth systems
options.definition: Understanding or predicting atmosphere, ocean, cryosphere, land, and coupled Earth-system behavior.

options.label: Materials & manufacturing
options.definition: Predicting material properties or behavior, and controlling or qualifying manufacturing processes.

options.label: Energy systems
options.definition: Generation, grid, storage, and fuel-cycle systems.

options.label: Nuclear & national security
options.definition: Stockpile, nonproliferation, treaty verification, and threat detection missions.

options.label: Biology & health
options.definition: Biological systems, biosecurity, and medical or public-health decisions.

options.label: Cyber & information systems
options.definition: Networks, software, and information environments.

options.label: Screening / triage
options.definition: Output prioritizes attention or generates hypotheses; a person decides what happens next.

options.label: Design / engineering
options.definition: Output informs design choices, parameters, or engineering trade-offs.

options.label: Qualification / certification
options.definition: Output supports a formal accept/reject or certification decision about a system or component.

options.label: Operational monitoring
options.definition: Output tracks the ongoing state of a system and triggers action when it changes.

options.label: Policy / planning
options.definition: Output informs policy, strategy, or resource allocation.

sections.title: Solution space
sections.help: Question → problem → phenomena. What the model is asked to do, and what kind of claim its answers will support.

questions.label: Question the model answers
questions.placeholder: e.g. Does AE data show that a component is damaged?

children.label: Classification
children.definition: Assign each case to one of a fixed set of classes.

children.label: Regression
children.definition: Estimate a continuous quantity for each case.
examples: September sea-ice extent from summer variables

children.label: Detection / anomaly
children.definition: Decide whether an event, object, or departure from normal is present.

children.label: Localization
children.definition: Estimate where something is in space or time.

children.label: Forecasting
children.definition: Predict future states of a time-evolving system.

children.label: Surrogate / emulation
children.definition: Replace an expensive simulation or experiment with a fast approximation.

children.label: Inverse problem / parameter estimation
children.definition: Infer causes, parameters, or inputs from observed effects.

children.label: Control / optimization
children.definition: Choose actions or designs that optimize an objective.

children.label: Structure discovery
children.definition: Find groups, modes, or relationships without labeled targets.
examples: Clustering AE hits into source mechanisms

children.label: Generation
children.definition: Produce new content: text, images, designs, or synthetic data.

options.label: Association
options.definition: Rung 1 of the causal ladder. Supports prediction under the conditions the data came from; says nothing about what happens if something is changed.

options.label: Intervention
options.hint: Reason about what happens if we act
options.definition: Rung 2. Supports reasoning about the effect of actions. Needs causal or structural assumptions beyond observational data.

options.label: Counterfactual
options.hint: Reason about what would have happened
options.definition: Rung 3. Supports reasoning about alternative histories for a specific case. Needs a structural causal model.

sections.title: Space of mappings
sections.help: The domain and range of the map the model learns or computes, and how it learns it.

children.label: Continuous
children.definition: Real-valued measurements.

children.label: Ordinal
children.definition: Ordered categories without a meaningful distance.

children.label: Categorical
children.definition: Unordered categories.

children.label: Time series
children.definition: Regularly sampled measurements over time, usually at low to moderate rates.

children.label: Raw waveform / signal
children.definition: High-rate sampled signals analyzed directly rather than through extracted features.

children.label: Event sequence
children.definition: Irregular, timestamped discrete events.

children.label: Image
children.definition: Regular 2-D or 3-D pixel or voxel grids.

children.label: Spatial field / mesh
children.definition: Physical fields on structured or unstructured meshes.

children.label: Point cloud
children.definition: Unordered sets of points in space.

children.label: Graph / network
children.definition: Entities and the relations between them.

children.label: Text
children.definition: Natural-language documents or records.

children.label: Binary
children.definition: Two classes.

children.label: Multiclass
children.definition: One of three or more exclusive classes.
examples: No damage / matrix cracking / fiber breakage / delamination

children.label: Multilabel
children.definition: Any subset of a set of labels.

children.label: Scalar
children.definition: One real-valued output.

children.label: Multivariate
children.definition: A fixed-length vector of real-valued outputs.

children.label: Field
children.definition: A spatial or spatio-temporal field.

children.label: Sequence
children.definition: A variable-length ordered output.

children.label: Set or graph
children.definition: A set, graph, or other combinatorial object.

children.label: Text
children.definition: Free-form natural language.

children.label: Images, signals, or designs
children.definition: Synthetic images, signals, or design candidates.

options.label: No learning
options.definition: The model is derived from theory and calibrated, not trained on data.

options.label: Supervised
options.definition: Learns from inputs paired with known targets.

options.label: Self- or semi-supervised
options.definition: Learns representations from unlabeled data, often fine-tuned with a few labels.

options.label: Unsupervised
options.definition: Finds structure without targets.

options.label: Reinforcement
options.definition: Learns a policy from rewards by interacting with an environment.

options.label: Generative
options.definition: Learns a data distribution in order to produce new samples.

sections.title: Numerical representation
sections.help: Where the model's knowledge comes from: explicit (governing equations), implicit (encoded structure such as symmetries or priors), and empirical (data).

children.label: Empirical only
children.hint: Learned from data; no encoded physics
children.definition: All knowledge comes from data. No explicit or implicit physical knowledge is built in.

children.label: Empirical with encoded structure
children.definition: Learned from data, with implicit knowledge built in: priors, symmetry or invariance, monotonicity, or architecture chosen to match the physics.

children.label: Physics-informed learning
children.definition: A learned model trained to satisfy governing equations as soft or hard constraints.

children.label: ML embedded in a simulator
children.definition: A mechanistic simulator with one or more learned components, such as closures or sub-grid models.

children.label: Surrogate of a simulator
children.definition: A learned model trained on simulation output to stand in for the simulator.
examples: Neural-operator emulator of a finite-element model

children.label: Grey-box / residual model
children.definition: A mechanistic model plus a learned correction for its residual error.
examples: Physics-based wave arrival model with learned correction

children.label: Explicit mechanistic
children.hint: Governing equations; data for calibration and validation
children.definition: Knowledge is explicit in governing equations. Data is used only to calibrate and validate.

questions.label: Data available for training and validation

options.label: Scarce
options.hint: Tens to hundreds of independent cases
options.definition: Few independent cases, as is typical of expensive experiments or rare events. Limits held-out validation and calibration.

options.label: Abundant
options.hint: Enough to hold out large test sets

sections.title: Semantics
sections.help: How the model's results are interpreted by the people who use them.

options.label: Descriptive
options.definition: Summarizes or characterizes observed data without inferring hidden states.
options.note: The ASA deck labels the AE example descriptive; the GCMM paper would call a damage classifier diagnostic, since it infers an unobserved state.

options.label: Diagnostic
options.hint: What state is it in, or why
options.definition: Infers an unobserved current state or its likely cause from observations.

options.label: Predictive
options.hint: What will it be for a new case
options.definition: Estimates outcomes for new cases under the same conditions as the training data.

options.label: Forecasting
options.definition: Projects a system's future states forward in time.

options.label: Prescriptive
options.definition: Recommends actions. Implies an interventional claim.

sections.title: Phenomena constraints
sections.help: What is known about the phenomena and built into the model, plus how the data is handled. The two are grouped separately because only the first encodes knowledge of the phenomena.

children.label: Conservation laws
children.definition: Mass, momentum, energy, or charge conservation enforced or checked.

children.label: Symmetry or invariance
children.definition: Invariance or equivariance to translation, rotation, scale, or sensor placement.

children.label: Monotonicity or shape
children.definition: Known monotone or convex relationships enforced.

children.label: Boundary or initial conditions
children.definition: Known boundary or initial conditions built into the model.

children.label: Physics-based regularization
children.definition: Governing-equation residuals added as a penalty during training.

children.label: Categorical encoding
children.definition: One-hot, ordinal, or target encoding of categorical inputs.
children.note: Listed as a phenomena constraint on slide 17 of the ASA deck; grouped here as data handling.

children.label: Normalization / scaling
children.definition: Standardizing or rescaling inputs.

children.label: Feature engineering
children.definition: Deriving features from raw data using domain knowledge.

children.label: Dimension reduction
children.definition: PCA, autoencoders, or feature selection before modeling.

children.label: Filtering / resampling
children.definition: Signal filtering, windowing, or resampling.

sections.title: Architecture / algorithm
sections.help: The model family you use or propose. Top levels span computational tools broadly; detailed sub-categories exist only for ML.

children.label: PDE solver
children.definition: Numerical solution of partial differential equations (FEM, FV, FD, spectral).

children.label: ODE / lumped system
children.definition: Ordinary differential equations or lumped-parameter models.

children.label: Agent-based model
children.definition: Individual agents with rules whose interactions produce system behavior.

children.label: Discrete-event simulation
children.definition: Systems modeled as sequences of events in time.

children.label: Linear / GLM
children.definition: Linear and generalized linear models.

children.label: Bayesian hierarchical model
children.definition: Probabilistic models with explicit priors and multilevel structure.

children.label: Time-series / state-space model
children.definition: ARIMA, Kalman filters, and other state-space models.

children.label: Tree ensemble
children.definition: Random forests and gradient-boosted trees.

children.label: Kernel method
children.definition: Support vector machines and kernel ridge regression.

children.label: Gaussian process
children.definition: Nonparametric Bayesian regression or classification.

children.label: Nearest neighbors
children.definition: Prediction from the most similar training cases.

children.label: Clustering / mixture model
children.definition: k-means, Gaussian mixtures, hierarchical and density-based clustering.

children.label: Feed-forward (MLP)
children.definition: Fully connected layers on fixed-length inputs.

children.label: Convolutional (CNN)
children.definition: Convolutions over grids such as signals, images, or fields.

children.label: Recurrent / transformer
children.definition: Sequence models: RNNs, LSTMs, and transformers trained for the task.

children.label: Graph neural network
children.definition: Message passing over graphs.

children.label: Autoencoder
children.definition: Learns a compressed representation by reconstructing its input.

children.label: Physics-informed neural network
children.definition: Neural network trained with governing-equation residuals in the loss.

children.label: Neural operator
children.definition: Learns maps between function spaces (FNO, DeepONet) to emulate PDE solutions.

children.label: Foundation model / LLM
children.definition: Large pretrained models used directly, prompted, or fine-tuned.

children.label: Diffusion model
children.definition: Generates samples by iterative denoising.

children.label: VAE / GAN
children.definition: Variational autoencoders and generative adversarial networks.

children.label: RL policy
children.definition: Policy or value-function learning (DQN, PPO, and similar).

sections.title: Your team
sections.help: Check the roles you already have. Anything recommended but unchecked is reported as a staffing gap.

consistency_checks.text: Classification problems produce categorical outputs. Check the output type under Space of mappings.
Regression problems produce continuous outputs. Check the output type under Space of mappings.
Generation problems produce generated content. Check the output type.
A generative learning setting usually produces generated or structured output. Check the output type.
Structure discovery normally uses unsupervised or self-supervised learning. Check the learning setting.
Control and optimization recommend actions, which makes the semantics prescriptive.
Forecasting problems normally have forecasting semantics. Check the Semantics ranking.
Prescriptive use recommends actions, which is an interventional claim. Check the kind of claim under Solution space.
An explicit mechanistic representation implies a mechanistic simulation (or a statistical model of it) as the model family.
A mechanistic simulation carries explicit knowledge, so the numerical representation should be mechanistic or hybrid.
A physics-informed neural network is physics-informed learning under Numerical representation.
Physics constraints mean the model carries more than empirical knowledge. Check Numerical representation.
A model that is not trained is normally explicit mechanistic. Check Numerical representation.
Clustering is unsupervised. Check the learning setting.
A neural or generative model trained on scarce data without encoded structure will be hard to validate and calibrate. Consider encoding known structure or a simpler model family.
Scarce data and expected shift together leave little room to validate across conditions empirically. Encoded physics or structure is the main lever for credibility here.
